name: aerojet-careers
description: Aerojet Aviation Careers Portal — Job listings, applications, admin dashboard

scripts.ci:all: bun run ci:lint && bun run ci:type-check && bun run ci:build && bun run ci:test

//ajv-note: No `ajv` override on purpose. @eslint/eslintrc requires ajv v6 (it passes the v6-only `missingRefs` option and expects the v6 CJS export shape), so forcing v8 crashes every `eslint` run with "Cannot set properties of undefined (setting 'defaultMeta')". Scoped overrides/resolutions did not stick: Bun kept the hoisted v8. The advisory (ReDoS via the `$data` option, >=7.0.0-alpha.0 <8.18.0) does not affect v6, and the vulnerable v8 copy is pulled only by @vercel/static-config, a dev-only deploy tool that never ships. Left to normal resolution: eslintrc keeps v6, everything else gets v8.
//path-to-regexp-undici-note: Not overridden on purpose. Both live only in the `vercel` CLI tree (deploy tooling) and `jsdom` (tests), and both exist at several majors at once: path-to-regexp at 6.1.0/6.3.0/8.2.0/8.3.0 (needs >=6.3.0 for the 6.x line and >=8.4.0 for the 8.x line) and undici from 5.28.4 up to 7.29.0 (clearing every advisory would require every copy to be >=6.28.0, i.e. a major bump inside the CLI). A single flat override cannot express per-major targets, and Bun ignored nested/scoped overrides here, so forcing one version would break the CLI for no production benefit. `vercel` is a devDependency (see //vercel-devDependency-note), so none of these copies reach the production dependency tree that the CI audit gate checks (`bun audit --production`).
//vercel-devDependency-note: The `vercel` CLI is deploy tooling, not an application runtime dependency: nothing under app/, components/, lib/ or scripts/ imports it. It used to sit in `dependencies`, which made the whole CLI tree (undici 5.x/7.x, path-to-regexp 6.x/8.x, @fastify/busboy) part of the production dependency surface, so `bun audit --production` reported 15 high-severity advisories that no production code could ever reach. Moving it to `devDependencies` keeps the install identical for CI and Vercel (both install devDependencies) while making the production audit surface reflect what actually ships.
//braces-note: Not overridden on purpose. `braces` 3.0.3 is the latest published release and is itself the affected version (GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm, <=3.0.3), so there is no patched version to move to. It is reached only through micromatch -> fast-glob -> @next/eslint-plugin-next / @ts-morph/common, i.e. the lint and codemod toolchain, and is therefore outside the production dependency tree that the CI audit gate checks.
